This Men’s Health Month, let’s make space for conversations that feel easier to start.

Health discussions, especially around fertility and reproductive health, are often delayed because they feel confusing, uncomfortable, or overwhelming.

But clarity, openness, and understanding can make a meaningful difference. When people feel informed instead of intimidated, they are more likely to seek answers early and take confident steps towards their health.

At Nova IVF Fertility, we believe empathy begins with making every health conversation feel simple, transparent, and easier to navigate.

Male fertility is often overlooked until the journey to parenthood takes longer than expected.

But fertility is not only about sperm count. Sperm quality, including movement and overall health, can also play an important role in conception.
Advanced techniques like Microfluidics help select healthier moving sperm during IVF treatment, supporting a more personalised approach to fertility care.
This Men's Health Month, let's encourage earlier conversations, timely evaluations, and greater awareness around male fertility health.

Some dreams take a little longer to come true.

They begin as quiet hopes, become whispered prayers, and one day turn into the most beautiful reality.
This Father’s Day, we’re celebrating every dad who held on to hope, believed through the waiting, and never gave up on his dream of a family.

In IVF, precision matters at every stage.

From the collection of eggs and sperm to embryo transfer, accurate identification and verification play an important role throughout the treatment journey.

RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) technology adds an additional layer of electronic witnessing by assigning unique identifiers to biological samples and tracking them through key stages of the IVF process. This helps strengthen traceability and supports laboratory protocols designed to minimise the possibility of mix-ups.
At Nova IVF Fertility, RFID-based witnessing is integrated into our IVF laboratory processes as part of our commitment to maintaining high standards of safety and care.

A diagnosis of azoospermia can feel overwhelming, especially when a semen analysis shows no sperm. For many men, it may seem like the end of the road to fatherhood.

However, in some cases, sperm may still be present within the testes and can sometimes be retrieved through specialised procedures such as TESA, TESE or Micro-TESE. These retrieved sperm may then be used in IVF/ICSI treatment, offering some couples an opportunity to pursue pregnancy using their own sperm and eggs.
This Men’s Health Month, let’s remember that the right diagnosis and expert evaluation can make all the difference.

Father's Day: AI Now Reading Sperm, Giving Hope of Fatherhood to Infertile Men
Dr. PGL Lalit Kumar, Head of Embryology and Scientific Director, Nova IVF Fertility

AI is revolutionizing sperm analysis in fertility clinics by offering more accurate and consistent assessments. While AI aids in identifying rare sperm cells and improving treatment outcomes, experts stress it should complement, not replace, clinical expertise. The adoption of AI in fertility care is increasing, enhancing the precision and efficiency of evaluations.

This Men’s Health Month, it’s important to remember that a man’s health extends beyond just himself.

Physical health, emotional well-being, lifestyle habits, and reproductive health can all influence not only his own future, but also the well-being of his partner and the family he hopes to build.
Small everyday choices, timely health check-ups, and greater awareness can make a meaningful difference over time. Prioritising health today is also an investment in healthier tomorrows for the generations ahead.
At Nova IVF Fertility, we believe conversations around fertility and reproductive health should include men equally because awareness and early action matter for everyone involved.

Sometimes, supporting your fertility doesn’t require long hours at the gym, just a few intentional moments through the day. Even short bursts of movement can begin to make a difference to how your body responds

Exercise snacking,” or quick intervals of activity, is linked to better hormone balance, improved circulation, and lower stress levels. When done consistently, these small efforts can support your body more effectively than a sedentary routine.
At Nova IVF Fertility, we guide you towards simple, sustainable habits that work with your lifestyle, helping you move forward, one step at a time.

Around 15–20 eggs begin developing in your ovaries each month.

But the body naturally selects just one dominant egg and asks the rest to stop growing.
This is a normal biological process, not a limitation.
In IVF, this process is supported differently, allowing multiple eggs to continue developing for better chances of conception.
At Nova IVF Fertility, we believe awareness of your body helps you make more informed fertility choices.

Sometimes what feels like falling behind is just the body and mind taking a different path than expected.

There are moments in the fertility journey when things feel uncertain, when progress feels slow, and when answers do not come easily.
But with the right guidance, clarity slowly replaces confusion and support makes all the difference.

At Nova IVF Fertility, we focus on bringing structure to that uncertainty through informed decisions, scientific analysis, personalised support and expert guidance.

What is SSG? 🌸

SSG (Saline Sonohysterography) is a special ultrasound test where saline is gently used to clearly see the inside of the uterus.

SSG helps detect:
✅ Uterine polyps
✅ Fibroids
✅ Adhesions or scars
✅ Causes of infertility
✅ Causes of recurrent pregnancy loss

A clear and healthy uterine cavity can improve the chances of implantation and pregnancy. Early diagnosis helps your fertility specialist plan the right treatment at the right time. 💛

At Sunrise Fertility & IVF Centre, we provide accurate fertility evaluation and personalized care for every couple’s parenthood journey.

When Should You Get an HSG Test? 🌸

An HSG (Hysterosalpingography) is a simple X-ray test that checks whether your fallopian tubes are open and evaluates the shape of your uterus. It is an important investigation for couples facing difficulty conceiving.

Your doctor may recommend an HSG if:
✅ You have been trying to conceive for 1 year without success (or 6 months if you are over 35)
✅ Pregnancy is not happening despite regular ovulation
✅ You are planning IUI treatment
✅ There is a suspicion of blocked fallopian tubes or unexplained infertility

Blocked fallopian tubes can prevent the egg and sperm from meeting, making natural conception difficult. Identifying the cause early helps your fertility specialist choose the most appropriate treatment.

💛 Early diagnosis leads to better fertility planning and improved chances of pregnancy.

What is Follicular Study? 🌸

Follicular study is a series of ultrasound scans done to track egg growth and identify the right time of ovulation.

It helps in:
✅ Knowing the exact ovulation day

**Strategies to Improve Egg Quality and Number of Eggs**

Egg quality and egg number are crucial factors for successful conception, whether natural or through IVF. Egg number mainly depends on age and ovarian reserve, while egg quality reflects the genetic and metabolic health of the egg. Although new eggs cannot be created, the quality of existing eggs can be improved by optimizing the body’s internal environment.

A healthy lifestyle forms the foundation of good egg health. A balanced diet rich in proteins, antioxidants, fruits, vegetables, nuts, and healthy fats helps reduce oxidative stress on eggs. Maintaining an ideal body weight, avoiding smoking, alcohol, and excess caffeine, and ensuring adequate sleep are equally important. Stress reduction through yoga, meditation, or regular physical activity supports hormonal balance.

Medical optimization also plays a key role. Treating thyroid disorders, insulin resistance, and hormonal imbalances improves ovulation and ovarian response. Supplements such as CoQ10, myo-inositol, vitamin D, and omega-3 fatty acids may enhance egg quality when taken under medical supervision.

In IVF, individualized stimulation protocols, correct dosing, and precise timing can improve the number of mature eggs retrieved. Ultimately, improving egg quality and number is a gradual process, and early, personalized fertility care offers the best chance of success.
How to Improve Endometrial Thickness:

For pregnancy to occur, the uterus needs a healthy inner lining called the endometrium, where the embryo attaches and grows. In some women, this lining remains thin despite medicines, hormones, or fertility treatments. A thin endometrium can reduce the chances of embryo implantation, especially during IVF.

Mesenchymal Stem Cells (MSCs) are an advanced treatment option for women who do not respond to routine therapies. These special cells have the ability to repair and regenerate damaged tissues. They are usually obtained from safe sources such as the placenta or umbilical cord.

When MSCs are introduced into the uterus, they help improve blood flow, reduce scarring, and promote the growth of healthy endometrial tissue. Unlike treatments that work temporarily, MSC therapy aims to improve the overall quality of the uterine lining.

This therapy may benefit women with very thin endometrium, scarring after infections or surgery, or repeated IVF failures due to poor endometrial growth. MSC therapy is considered a specialized option and is recommended only after proper evaluation and counseling by a fertility specialist.
